batchName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE) - Hard Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE)

questions.question: According to a writer alive at the time, how did Cleopatra kill herself?
options: By leaping from the top of her tomb
By drinking a cup of hemlock
By drowning herself in the Nile
By falling on a sword as Antony had done
By a snake's bite or poisoned ointment
By starving herself in her tomb
questions.explanation: A contemporary writer gave a snake's bite or poisoned ointment as the cause. She died on 12 August 30 BC, rather than be paraded in Octavian's triumph.
questions.sourceQuote: On 12 August 30 BC she killed herself, by a snake's bite or poisoned ointment according to a writer alive at the time.

questions.question: Which territories did Antony give Cleopatra so she could build a fleet? (select all that apply)
options: Judaea
Cyprus
Sicily
Cilicia
Armenia
Crete
questions.explanation: Antony gave her land in Cyprus and Cilicia. He also acknowledged twins she bore him in 40 BC, and the relationship was deeply unpopular in Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: Antony later acknowledged twins she bore him in 40 BC and fathered a son with her, and he gave her territory in Cyprus and Cilicia, whose timber could build a fleet.

questions.question: In 34 BC Antony paraded the captured king of Armenia through Alexandria in a procession honouring which god?
options: Serapis
Jupiter
Hercules
Isis
Dionysus
Apollo
questions.explanation: The procession honoured Dionysus. The parade, followed by the Donations of Alexandria, handed Octavian plenty of propaganda ammunition.
questions.sourceQuote: In 34 BC he tricked the king of Armenia into captivity and paraded him through Alexandria, Egypt's capital, in a procession honouring the god Dionysus.

questions.question: What crucial mistake contributed to Antony's failure in Parthia in 36 BC?
options: He left his cavalry behind in Egypt
He raced ahead of his slow siege engines, which were destroyed
He trusted a Parthian prince's offer of surrender
He invaded in winter without supplies
He kept waiting for Octavian's promised troops
He split his army between Armenia and Syria
questions.explanation: With his siege engines lost and his Armenian ally gone, Antony endured a 27-day retreat under horse-archer attack and lost about a third of his men.
questions.sourceQuote: With sixteen legions he raced ahead of his slow siege engines, which the enemy then destroyed.

questions.question: Why did the surviving assassin offer battle again three weeks after the first clash at Philippi?
options: The Senate ordered him to attack
Parthian reinforcements had arrived
Octavian had fallen gravely ill
A shipment of eastern silver had arrived
Antony challenged him to single combat
He feared his troops would desert
questions.explanation: Fearing desertions, he fought again on 23 October 42 BC and was crushed by the combined Caesarian armies, after which he took his own life.
questions.sourceQuote: Three weeks later, on 23 October 42 BC, the surviving assassin offered battle again, fearing desertions.

questions.question: Which powers did the triumvirs hold under their arrangement? (select all that apply)
options: Abolishing the Senate
Appointing every magistrate
Naming their own successors
Holding office for life
Punishing without right of appeal
Making binding decrees
questions.explanation: The triumvirs could decree, overrule governors, punish without appeal and appoint all magistrates, but their power was granted for five years, not for life. Official records even listed them above the consuls.
questions.sourceQuote: The three could make binding decrees, overrule any governor, punish without right of appeal, and appoint every magistrate.

questions.question: What terms did the triumvirs grant their enemy in Sicily when they made peace in 39 BC?
options: A place on the board as a fourth triumvir
Control of Africa in exchange for Lepidus
Marriage to Octavian's widowed sister
Pardon only if he surrendered his fleet
A consulship and command of Spain
Freedom for his runaway slaves and veterans' rewards for his men
questions.explanation: The peace freed his runaway slaves and gave his soldiers veterans' rewards. His naval blockade had worsened a famine in Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: In 39 BC the triumvirs also made peace with their enemy in Sicily, freeing his runaway slaves and giving his soldiers veterans' rewards.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the Senate's victory over Antony at Mutina in April 43 BC?
options: Antony fled by sea to Egypt
Both consuls died and Octavian marched on Rome
Lepidus took command of the Senate's army
The assassins returned to Rome in triumph
Octavian was named dictator by the Senate
Antony was captured and executed
questions.explanation: The Senate won and declared Antony a public enemy, but both consuls died in the fighting, leaving Octavian free to march on Rome and claim power.
questions.sourceQuote: But both consuls died in the fighting, and Octavian marched on Rome to claim power for himself.

questions.question: In the dispute over how many died in the proscriptions, which historians tend to favour the higher numbers?
options: Those who believe Octavian opposed the killings
Those who count only senators as victims
Those who trust the triumvirs' declaration
Those who think the triumvirs mainly wanted money
Those who rely on Antony's own records
Those who think revenge for Caesar drove the lists
questions.explanation: Seeing money as the main motive fits a larger toll. One modern study instead settles on about 300 names, split evenly between senators and knights.
questions.sourceQuote: Historians who think the triumvirs mainly wanted money tend to favour the higher numbers.

questions.question: What weakened Antony's trapped army at Actium before the sea battle?
options: Malaria and desertion
Plague carried from Egypt
An earthquake that wrecked the camp
Cleopatra recalling her troops
Famine caused by a Parthian raid
A mutiny over unpaid wages
questions.explanation: After Octavian's admiral cut his supply lines, Antony's camp was ravaged by malaria and desertion. A defecting general even handed over his battle plan.
questions.sourceQuote: Trapped, Antony's camp was ravaged by malaria and desertion.
